parameters.name: Enable
parameters.description: Enables or disables the time client.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: Status of Time support for this client. {{enum}}

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Specifies in which mode the NTP client must be run. {{enum}}

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description: Specify the port used to send NTP packets. {{bibref|RFC5905|Section 7.2}}

parameters.name: IPVersion
parameters.description: Specifies the IP protocol version, following the definitions in {{bibref|IANA-ipversionnumbers}}. Valid values are: {{range}}.

parameters.name: ServerInUse
parameters.description: Specifies the server currently used for time synchronization. The value reported is the exact server entry as configured in the {{param|Servers}} parameter. If the server is specified as a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) in the {{param|Servers}} parameter, the configured FQDN will be reported here, not the resolved IP address or CNAME.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.description: Specifies the supported NTP version. Possible versions are 1-4.

parameters.name: Servers
parameters.description: Points to a CSV list of NTP servers or pools. A NTP server can either be specified as an IP address or a host name. It is expected that the NTP client resolves multiple addresses which can change over time when {{param|ResolveAddresses}} is enabled.

parameters.name: ResolveAddresses
parameters.description: When this option is enabled the NTP client must resolve the multiple addresses associated with the host name(s) that are specified in the {{param|Servers}} field.

parameters.name: ResolveMaxAddresses
parameters.description: When {{param|ResolveAddresses}} is enabled, This parameter specifies the maximum number of IP addresses that the NTP client can resolve. 0 means that all addresses must be resolved.

parameters.name: Peer
parameters.description: Use symmetric active association mode. This device may provide synchronization to the configured NTP server.

parameters.name: MinPoll
parameters.description: This is the minimum polling interval, in {{units}} to the power of two, allowed by any peer of the Internet system, currently set to 6 (64 seconds). {{bibref|RFC5905|Section 7.2}}

parameters.name: MaxPoll
parameters.description: This is the maximum polling interval, in {{units}} to the power of two, allowed by any peer of the Internet system, currently set to 10 (1024 seconds) {{bibref|RFC5905|Section 7.2}}

parameters.name: IBurst
parameters.description: If the {{param}} parameter is enabled, and this is the first packet sent when the server has been unreachable, the client sends a burst. This is useful to quickly reduce the synchronization distance below the distance threshold and synchronize the clock. {{bibref|RFC5905}}.

parameters.name: Burst
parameters.description: If the {{param}} parameter is enabled and the server is reachable and a valid source of synchronization is available, the client sends a burst of BCOUNT (8) packets at each poll interval. The interval between packets in the burst is two seconds. This is useful to accurately measure jitter with long poll intervals. {{bibref|RFC5905}}.

parameters.name: Interface
parameters.description: The IP Interface associated with the ''Client'' entry.

parameters.name: BindType
parameters.description: Specifies how the client sockets are bound. {{enum}}

object.description: This object contains parameters relating to an time client instance.
